shared_elements: shallow low-relief carving on weathered stone
horizontal band or register dividing the surface
justification: Both surfaces bear shallow, schematic low-relief motifs — notably rounded discs/ovals and long curved arcs — with at least one horizontal dividing band organising the field, and both are heavily weathered stone. But A is a flat rectangular block with motifs laid out in stacked horizontal registers read left-to-right, whereas B is a three-dimensional standing figure whose carvings are distributed vertically over a modelled head and torso, so the compositional logic and the manner of cutting (fine linear outlines versus broad rounded bosses) differ substantially.
